caption: Simple road tiles alone cannot create branches or dead ends.
content: We call a road with no branches @T{forest_road.3.dlr} or dead ends @T{forest_road.1.r} a @b{simple road}.

A road made by connecting simple road tiles @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} is always a simple road.
In other words, simple road tiles alone can never create branches or dead ends.
Using this fact, you can easily determine that an Area @b{cannot be completed} just by looking at @b{the number of roads entering the Area}.

content.caption: Example 1
content: Assuming your available road tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} and their rotations, let's solve this Area.

Only one road enters this Area.
Even if you extend this road using the available simple road tiles, you cannot close it. No matter how you lay out the road, there will always be a cell @m{unsatisfied} where no tile can be placed. Therefore, this Area cannot be completed.
In general, when you can only create simple roads, @b{an Area with exactly one road entering it cannot be completed}.

content.caption: Example 2
content: Assuming your available road tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} and their rotations, let's solve this Area.

Three roads enter this Area.
Since the available simple road tiles cannot create branches, these roads cannot all be connected into a single network. Therefore, the @g{rule/complete_block/road}{condition for completing an Area involving roads} cannot be met, so this Area cannot be completed.
In general, when you can only create simple roads, @b{an Area with three or more roads entering it cannot be completed}.
